## Historical audit: H0005

**Scope.** Student trace, chunk 2 of 3 only. The inferred goal was an opt-in Obsidian Linter rule that generates or updates a marker-delimited table of contents; the student’s own restatement is visible, but the original request is not in this chunk (main_agent:event:142). This is a software task, not a scene task.

**Source for all event citations:** H0005, `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_obsidian_a1_vm8_20261120_r1/infer_logs/obsidian-linter-auto-table-of-contents/turn_1/trajs.json`. Offsets below refer to the supplied event observations.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Exploration | The student inspected rule defaults and existing conventions, including settings initialization and regex-list usage (events 89–98). It considered competing literal-exclusion semantics before choosing case-insensitive substring matching; that was an interpretation, not a verified requirement (event 99). |
| Changes | Created branch `feat/auto-toc` at the same commit as `master`, with a clean initial tree (event 102). Created a test file (event 105) and a rule implementing marker detection, heading filtering, anchors, list options and ignore types (event 117, characters [0,16137)). Added English locale descriptions and enum labels (events 122 [0,54558), 125 [0,52441)). |
| Validation | Before implementation, the new Jest suite failed to import the missing module and ran zero tests (event 108). Later, its 17 authored cases passed, with a forced-worker-exit warning (event 144). The full local suite reported 60 suites and 1,211 tests passed, also with that warning (event 169). These tests include the student’s own expectations, not independent confirmation of the specification. |
| Other checks | Type-check output included errors in the new tests’ partial option objects and other project/dependency files (event 129); the student subsequently cast nine test options to `any` (events 140–141). Build output reported an unresolved `micromark-extension-frontmatter` dependency (event 149). ESLint found an unused import, which was removed; the re-lint returned no output (events 148, 152 [0,16911), 157). |
| Later work | Three further tests were added, then an expected blank line was edited (events 181 [0,10933), 183). The latter edit’s result and a subsequent test run are not visible in this chunk. |

**Formal outcome.** Supplied inventory metadata records `not_solved`, 0/41 fail-to-pass and 1131/1131 pass-to-pass, and a nonempty 18,739-byte patch. This is formal failure despite local test passes; the visible excerpt does not establish the cause. The build dependency error is a technical obstacle, not proof of the evaluation failure. The student hypothesized it was pre-existing, but no clean-baseline build is shown.

**Teacher input and adoption.** No teacher message, delivered hint, or evidence of adoption appears in this chunk. An archived system-prompt link in metadata establishes availability only, not receipt. Earlier or later input cannot be determined from this excerpt.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, self-authored tests can validate an implementation against its own interpretation while missing external requirements; separate baseline failures from change-induced failures before assigning cause. Task-specific unresolved hypotheses include substring versus exact exclusions, marker/EOF whitespace, and displayed link formatting. No visible evaluator failure details connect any one of these to the 0/41 result. Later changes, the final patch contents, and the full-suite result after the added tests remain unobserved here.
